notes: "Some people looked at a man called Rozaine." — 'looked at' does not tell an A1 reader that people suspected him. Consider: "Some people said, 'Maybe Rozaine is Lupin!'"

"But Rozaine showed his papers to everyone." — 'papers' in the sense of identity documents may not be clear at A1; "showed his passport" is simpler. Other levels say he showed them to the captain/officers; 'to the captain' would also be more consistent.
Vocabulary is otherwise within reach (message, across, edge are borderline but clear from context). Grammar stays in present/past simple.
"For years, he looked for Lupin." — past simple for an ongoing span reads a little flat; "For years, he tried to catch Lupin." sounds more natural within the A2 grammar limit.
"People looked at each other with fear." — slightly stilted; "People were afraid and watched each other." is more natural.
"Nelly took one step to the side." — vaguer than other levels; "Nelly took one step to the edge of the water." makes the drop easier to picture.
No passive or conditionals found; relative clauses and past continuous are fine for B1. Plot, order and ending match the original.

issues.quote: 3. Why was the camera important to Ganimard? — *It held the jewels and money that proved Lupin's guilt
issues.problem: The B2 text only ever says the jewels were hidden in the camera; money is never mentioned, so the keyed answer asserts a fact the reader cannot find in the text.
issues.fix: Change the keyed option to: "It held the jewels that proved Lupin's guilt".

notes: Second conditional ("If Ganimard found that camera, he would have all the proof he needed.") is fine at B2. Rozaine's reward is a faithful detail.

issues.quote: A good many gentlemen on board would gladly have claimed her attention, yet for reasons I did not fully deserve she seemed to prefer mine.
issues.problem: One deserves a favour, not 'reasons'; the phrase is semantically off and a careful reader trips on it.
issues.fix: "...yet, by a kindness I did not fully deserve, she seemed to prefer mine." (or "for reasons I never fully understood")

issues.quote: Had Ganimard opened that camera, he would have held every proof he needed.
issues.problem: 'proof' in this sense is uncountable, and 'held every proof' is not idiomatic.
issues.fix: "Had Ganimard opened that camera, he would have had all the proof he needed."

notes: "laid before him his papers, his letters and every other proof of his identity he could find" — acceptable but stiff; "every other document that could prove who he was" reads more smoothly.
Ending and Lupin's reflection on Nelly's choice are faithful to Leblanc's story; tone is genuinely literary.

summary: A faithful, age-appropriate retelling of Leblanc's story at every level, with A1-B1 clean. B2 fails on a quiz key that mentions money the text never states, and C1 fails on two unidiomatic phrases ('for reasons I did not fully deserve', 'held every proof he needed'); all three are one-line fixes.
